newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state issues first trial digital TV permits.
newsitem.headline: German state issues first trial digital TV permits.

text.p: The first digital television licences have been issued in Germany, clearing the way for a summer trial run, media officials in the western state of Rhineland-Palatinate said on Tuesday.

Digital service DF1, pay television channel Premiere and programming package MultiThematiques received broadcasting permits and cable slots from the state private broadcasting authority (LPR) for a pilot digital television service.

The LPR said that home shopping channels QVC and Homeorder Television had also been approved to join in the digital television experiment. A maximum of 15 channels are available on the state's cable band for digital television, the LPR said.

"With the selection of participants...and the distribution of the first permits, the LPR has fulfilled the broadcasting requirements for the launch of digital television," the authority said in a statement.
But the LPR accused cable network administrator Deutsche Telekom of dragging its feet over the project.

"It is still the case that cable network managers, above all (Deutsche) Telekom, have done nothing to insure that digital programmes could be broadcast as soon as technologically possible," the authority said.
The LPR said the decoder boxes necessary to receive digital channels on standard television were not ready, but said they would be available by the start of the summer trial.

Top media executives, state politicians and Deutsche Telekom chairman Ron Sommer will hold meetings on May 20 to attempt to resolve an industry dispute over digital television and reorganisation of cable TV networks in Germany.
